title: Het cerebellum als belangrijke neurale basis voor motorische reserve tijdens gezond ouder worden
abstract: Aging is an inevitable biological process accompanied by widespread structural and functional changes in both the body and the brain. In the motor domain, aging is typically associated with declines in movement precision, speed, balance, and adaptability, which are commonly attributed to sensory degradation, reduced muscle strength, and neural degeneration. However, converging evidence indicates that not all motor control mechanisms are equally affected by aging. In particular, processes involved in predictive and anticipatory motor control appear to be relatively preserved across the adult lifespan. Predictive motor control relies on neural processes that enable the brain to anticipate the sensory consequences of motor commands and to prepare appropriate actions before errors occur. The cerebellum is widely recognized as playing a key role in these predictive processes, supporting functions such as anticipatory muscle activation, motor timing, sensorimotor prediction, and motor adaptation. Although the precise computational principles underlying cerebellar function remain debated, converging evidence indicates that it contributes critically to the fine-tuning and coordination of movement. If such cerebellar-dependent predictive processes are maintained during aging despite widespread neural degeneration, this may reflect the existence of a cerebellar motor reserve that supports stable motor function into advanced age. The primary aim of this research was to systematically investigate age-related changes in cerebellar-specific motor functions and to identify potential mechanisms underlying their preservation. To this end, we conducted a large cross-sectional study including healthy young adults, older adults, and adults aged 80 years and older. Participants completed an extensive behavioral battery comprising motor and cognitive tasks, in combination with structural and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and assessments of physical fitness. The behavioral task battery was designed to target specifically cerebellar-dependent predictive processes, while also including more general motor and cognitive measures to assess the specificity and generalizability of potential preservation effects. Crucially, to meaningfully assess concepts such as reserve and resilience, it is essential to challenge the system sufficiently, since maintained performance under low task demands does not necessarily imply maintained underlying control mechanisms. Therefore, in several tasks, difficulty levels were systematically increased to probe performance under heightened demands, such that we could measure resilience as the degree to which performance deteriorated when task demands increased. The results revealed a clear and consistent pattern. Cerebellar-specific motor outcomes were remarkably maintained across the lifespan, including in participants aged 80 years and older. Maintained functions included anticipatory muscle timing and activation during multi-joint movements, motor timing precision, anticipatory eye velocity, sensory attenuation, and implicit motor adaptation. Across these outcome measures, performance did not differ significantly between younger, older, and older-old adults. Importantly, for those task outcomes for which resilience could be evaluated, these cerebellar-specific functions remained maintained under increased task demands, indicating a high degree of resilience in processes strongly linked to cerebellar function. One notable exception was smooth pursuit-saccade coordination, which showed age-related decline. However, it is important to recognize that these so-called cerebellar-specific outcome measures may not purely reflect cerebellar function, and their specificity remains uncertain. In contrast, motor control processes extending beyond cerebellar feedforward mechanisms showed pronounced age-related deterioration. Although anticipatory control remained intact, older adults exhibited increased movement inaccuracies during later phases of movement, indicating impaired feedback-based control. Similarly, postural balance performance declined with age, particularly when task demands were increased. These findings demonstrate a dissociation between maintained predictive motor control and vulnerable feedback-based and general sensorimotor processes. This pattern of maintenance did not extend to the cognitive domain. Age-related declines were observed both in a cerebellar-specific cognitive measure derived from a mental rotation task and in a general cognitive measure based on working memory performance. Notably, decline in the cerebellar-related cognitive measure emerged more gradually and became most pronounced only in adults over 80 years of age, whereas general cognitive decline was already evident in the younger older-adult group and increased further with age. While these findings suggest that the cerebellar reserve may be primarily expressed in motor rather than cognitive functions, this interpretation should be made with caution, as it is based on a single cognitive paradigm. Across tasks that included increased task demands, resilience measures were not correlated with one another and were not associated with maintained cerebellar-specific motor outcomes, indicating that resilience was largely task-specific and did not generalize across domains. Moreover, structural and functional neuroimaging measures failed to explain maintained motor performance. Neither cerebellar grey matter volume nor resting-state functional connectivity within or between cerebellar regions predicted task outcomes or resilience. Similarly, connectivity within and between cortical networks, as well as cortico-cerebellar connectivity, including relatively preserved connectivity between the somatomotor cortex and the cerebellum, did not account for maintained cerebellar motor function. Physical fitness measures were also unrelated to performance and resilience. Taken together, these findings provide converging evidence for the existence of a cerebellar motor reserve: a resilient predictive motor control system that remains functionally intact across healthy aging, even into advanced old age and under increased task demands. This maintenance occurs despite clear age-related deterioration in cerebellar structure and widespread reorganization of brain networks. At the same time, the present findings highlight a critical unresolved issue: although the cerebellar motor reserve is clearly manifest at the behavioral level, its biological and experiential foundations remain unknown. Future research should therefore focus on uncovering the mechanisms that feed this cerebellar motor reserve. Promising directions include examining task-evoked cerebellar activity and connectivity rather than resting-state measures alone, exploring whether cerebellar motor reserve offers protection in contexts of neurological disease, injury, or rehabilitation, and identifying behavioral, experiential, or developmental factors that may seed or strengthen this reserve across the lifespan. A better understanding of the mechanisms supporting cerebellar motor reserve may ultimately inform interventions aimed at maintaining autonomy and functional capacity in older populations.
authors: Anouck Matthijs

title: Urine metabolomics reveals key pathways supporting neuronal regeneration and consciousness recovery in disorders of consciousness
abstract: Disorders of consciousness (DoC) are debilitating conditions resulting from severe brain injury, requiring not only structural preservation but also active neuronal regeneration for recovery. These regenerative processes are metabolically demanding and can be tracked through systemic metabolic changes. Urine metabolomics provides a non-invasive approach to identifying metabolic signatures linked to neural recovery. This study aimed to determine whether urinary metabolic profiles reflect clinical classifications in DoC and identify pathways associated with neuronal regeneration and consciousness recovery. Urine samples from 37 DoC patients were analyzed using untargeted metabolomics. Patients were categorized by etiology, diagnosis, and prognosis. Statistical and pathway enrichment analyses identified group-specific metabolic alterations. Urine metabolomics revealed distinct metabolic patterns across etiologies, consciousness levels, and prognoses. Pyrimidine, nitrogen, and arginine metabolism were elevated in traumatic brain injury (TBI) patients, potentially reflecting sustained oxidative stress and regeneration. Patients with improved outcomes exhibited alterations in amino acid and tryptophan metabolism, suggesting enhanced neuroplasticity. Several metabolites showed strong predictive value for recovery. Urinary metabolic profiles reflect both clinical classification and underlying regenerative activity in DoC. TBI patients may benefit from chronic oxidative stress that influences neural remodeling, while patients with higher consciousness levels exhibit ascorbate-related dopaminergic metabolic patterns that may facilitate a positive feedback loop for recovery. Urine metabolomics is a practical, non-invasive approach to identify biomarkers and pathways associated with neuronal regeneration and consciousness recovery in DoC. Beyond prognostic utility, these metabolic signatures provide mechanistic clues to the metabolic–neurorepair processes that may enable large-scale network reactivation and the return of consciousness, warranting longitudinal validation and targeted pathway testing.
authors: Long Xu, Qianqian Ge, Hezhen Lu, Chen He, Hao Li et al.

title: MK-801- and memantine-induced locomotor hyperactivity is attenuated by conditional loss of dopamine D2 receptors in select forebrain neurons
abstract: Disruption of cerebral cortical interneuron maturation has been implicated in the pathophysiology of schizophrenia, and NMDA receptor antagonists are widely used to model psychosis-relevant behavioral phenotypes in rodents. Dopamine D2 receptors (D2Rs) are expressed on cortical GABAergic interneurons derived from the medial ganglionic eminence (MGE), where they regulate inhibitory circuit function during development and in adulthood. Whether D2R signaling on MGE-derived interneurons gates the locomotor and stereotypic responses to NMDA receptor antagonism has not been established. Here, we used mice with conditional deletion of D2Rs from developing Nkx2.1-lineage GABAergic interneurons (D2R-cKO) to examine this question across a dose-response range of MK-801 (0.1, 0.3, and 0.6 mg/kg) and a single dose of memantine (30 mg/kg), using a three-day open-field protocol. D2R-cKO mice and littermate controls did not differ in baseline locomotion or within-session or between-session habituation, confirming intact basal motor function. Following MK-801, D2R-cKO mice exhibited significantly blunted locomotor hyperactivity at the two behaviorally active doses (0.3 and 0.6 mg/kg), with no genotype difference at the lowest dose. Vertical activity echoed the horizontal locomotor activity findings. This locomotor attenuation was fully replicated with a second NMDA receptor antagonist, memantine, in an independent cohort. In contrast, drug-induced behavioral stereotypies were relatively less impacted than horizontal locomotion or rearing. In contrast, biological sex strongly influenced stereotypic behavior, with males showing higher counts than females across active doses but did not have effects on locomotion. Novel components of the current study include a robust dose-response characterization, the documentation of a behavioral dissociation between locomotion and stereotypy, and the replication of the phenotype using a pharmacologically distinct NMDA receptor antagonist. These findings demonstrate that D2R signaling within MGE-derived GABAergic neurons modulates the locomotor component of NMDA antagonist-induced behavioral activation.
authors: Yasmeena Thabet, Samantha E. Neville, Aisha O. Shafau, Devon L. Graham, Gregg D. Stanwood

title: Deletion or immunotherapeutic blockade of FcγRIIb (CD32b) impairs α-Syn propagation in vivo
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD), the most prevalent neurodegenerative movement disorder, is characterised by widespread alpha-synuclein (α-Syn) pathology in the brain and the progressive degeneration of nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons. Experimental and clinicopathological data support a templated, prion-like component to α-Syn spread; however, the cellular mechanisms governing fibril uptake and intercellular transmission remain incompletely defined. Fc gamma receptor IIb (FcγRIIb or CD32b), the sole cross-species inhibitory Fcγ receptor, has been implicated in α-Syn internalisation in vitro, though its contribution to α-Syn propagation in vivo is not well established. Here, we examine the role of FcγRIIb in α-Syn seeding, propagation, and neurotoxicity in vivo using the preformed fibril (PFF) α-Syn intracranial injection model in mice. Genetic ablation of murine FcγRII reduced phosphorylated α-Syn (pα-Syn) burden and anatomical distribution across multiple brain regions at 90 days post-PFF injection, consistent with impaired development of Lewy-like pathology. Attenuated pα-Syn pathology was accompanied by reduced microglial reactivity, preservation of nigrostriatal dopaminergic integrity, and protection from PFF-associated motor and exploratory deficits. In parallel, pharmacological blockade of human (h) FcγRIIb using monoclonal antibodies reduced acute-phase pα-Syn accumulation in hFcγRIIb-transgenic mice following PFF challenge. Collectively, these findings identify FcγRIIb as a critical regulator of α-Syn propagation in vivo and support receptor-targeted blockade as a mechanistically distinct and therapeutically tractable strategy for modifying disease progression in PD and related α-synucleinopathies.
authors: James M. Hennegan, Michael J. Hurley, Matthew Colley, Kerry L. Cox, Leon R. Douglas et al.

title: 多层级集群涌现-前额叶统合模型:从躯体内稳态信号到意识体验的完整闭环框架 Multi-level Cluster Emergence - Prefrontal Cortex Integration Model (MCE-PFC): A Complete Closed-Loop Framework From Somatic Homeostatic Signals to Conscious Experience
abstract: 作者:郭洋洋Author: Guo YangyangORCID:0009-0006-6669-1790Contact email:gyy-goes@foxmail.comPublication Type: PreprintSubmission Date: September 25, 2026Version: v1.0 Final Bilingual EditionPreprint DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22954675Open Access License: CC BY 4.0 摘要 Abstract 意识是认知科学与神经科学领域的核心难题。当前主流意识理论分别从脑内模块竞争、躯体信号根源、神经元集群选择、顶层执行控制等单一维度展开研究,普遍存在层级断裂、维度混淆、解释域狭窄的局限——既缺乏从细胞-器官-脑的完整纵向涌现链条,也未能清晰区分神经结构层级与主观体验层面的差异,更无法用单一框架同时解释念头自发涌现、心理内耗、共情融合三类核心心智现象。 Consciousness is a core challenge in the fields of cognitive science and neuroscience. Current mainstream theories of consciousness conduct research from single dimensions such as intracerebral module competition, somatic signal origins, neuronal cluster selection, and top-down executive control. They generally suffer from three limitations: hierarchical fracture, dimensional confusion, and narrow explanatory scope. Specifically, they lack a complete vertical emergence chain from cells to organs and then to the brain; fail to clearly distinguish between neural structural hierarchies and subjective experience levels; and cannot simultaneously explain three core mental phenomena—spontaneous emergence of thoughts, psychological internal friction, and empathic fusion—within a single framework. 本文通过整合全局工作空间理论、躯体标记假说、神经达尔文主义与前额叶执行功能理论,构建了多层级集群涌现-前额叶统合模型(MCE-PFC)。该模型提出:意识产生于“躯体集群内稳态信号涌现→潜意识神经集群竞争筛选→前额叶主意识统合”的三层级递进过程;所有念头与欲望的终极驱动源是躯体系统的内稳态偏差;结构层面前额叶与底层脑区存在永久的功能层级差异,体验层面二者可发生临时的神经同频共振,二者属于不同维度,互不矛盾。 By integrating Global Workspace Theory, Somatic Marker Hypothesis, Neural Darwinism, and Prefrontal Executive Function Theory, this paper constructs the Multi-level Cluster Emergence - Prefrontal Cortex Integration Model (MCE-PFC). The model proposes that consciousness arises from a three-stage progressive process: emergence of homeostatic signals from somatic clusters → competitive screening of subconscious neural clusters → integration of primary consciousness by the prefrontal cortex. The ultimate driving source of all thoughts and desires is the homeostatic deviation of the somatic system. At the structural level, there exists a permanent functional hierarchy between the prefrontal cortex and lower brain regions; at the experiential level, temporary neural synchronized resonance can occur between them. The two belong to different dimensions and are not mutually contradictory. 该模型用单一机制同时解释了正常意识运作、心理内耗、共情平静三类典型状态,弥补了现有理论的层级缺口与维度混淆问题,并提出5项可通过神经影像与行为实验验证的可证伪命题,为意识研究、临床心理干预、心智训练实践及认知因果学体系提供了统一的底层机制框架。 This model explains three typical states—normal conscious functioning, psychological internal friction, and empathic calm—with a single mechanism, addressing the hierarchical gaps and dimensional confusion in existing theories. It also puts forward five falsifiable propositions verifiable through neuroimaging and behavioral experiments, providing a unified underlying mechanistic framework for consciousness research, clinical psychological intervention, mental training practice, and the system of cognitive causality. 关键词:意识涌现;躯体标记;前额叶统合;集群竞争;内耗机制;认知因果学Keywords: consciousness emergence; somatic marker; prefrontal integration; cluster competition; internal friction mechanism; cognitive causality
